description: Class-A2: a protected path nested inside a list/dict structure under an arbitrary key in an MCP tool_input. Pre-fix, ``write_guard``'s MCP branch only inspected a fixed set of canonical top-level fields (``path``/``file_path``/``source``/``destination``). A batch-shaped MCP write — ``{files:[{path: <protected>}]}``, ``{batch:{files:[{path}]}}``, ``{edits:[{file:{path}}]}``, or any deeper nesting under a non-canonical key — placed the protected path where the field scan never looked, so the write was ALLOWED. This was a LIVE bypass: real MCP filesystem servers expose batch/edit verbs with exactly this shape. The fix: a depth/node-bounded, KEY-AGNOSTIC leaf-walk (``_hook_utils.iter_mcp_path_leaves`` + FS-free ``normalize_path_str``) that yields every leaf in the payload and protected-checks each, skipping only the casefolded ``MCP_CONTENT_KEYS`` (file bodies), failing CLOSED on ``MCPPayloadUnverifiable`` past the depth/node bound. write_guard walks key-agnostic (an under-fire is a security fail-open); plan_guard gates on ``key in MCP_PATH_FIELDS`` (severity-matched). This is the regression gate that keeps the nested-MCP-extraction class fixed.
documented_in: tests/test_write_guard.py::TestClassA2MCPLeafWalk (end-to-end nested-MCP extraction against the real check_mcp)
